newsitem.title: USA: Progenitor licenses technology to Amgen.
newsitem.headline: Progenitor licenses technology to Amgen.

text.p: Progenitor Inc, a unit of Interneuron Pharmaceuticals Inc, on Monday said it has licensed its leptin receptor technology to Amgen Inc for a $500,000 licensing fee and certain other fees.

The agreement also calls for Amgen to purchase $5.5 million of Progenitor common stock if that company launches an initial public offer. Also, Progenitor could receive payments of as much as $22 million if certain development and regulatory milestones are achieved.
Interneuron stock closed off 2-1/8 at 25-7/8. Amgen shares ended trading 3/8 lower at 56-3/4.
Leptin is a naturally-occurring hormone produced by fat cells. It is believed to help control the amount of body fat and overall body weight by regulating appetite and metabolism.
Under the terms of the deal, Amgen gains an exclusive worldwide license for leptin receptor technology for human therapeutic, diagnostic and prophylactic uses.
Progenitor retains exclusive rights for ex vivo ligand screening, small molecule screening and cell sorting.
Progenitor also retains exclusive rights for all human uses of leptin receptor DNA anti-sense molecules, and in vivo human uses of leptin receptor-specific antibodies.
